label: Native iOS engineering
summary: Ship Swift and SwiftUI work that is built, tested and observed — real xcodebuild runs, XCTest, simulator verification, and honest reporting of device-only gates.

registry_skills.name: ios-dev
registry_skills.note: Entry point for Apple work: coordinates the guides, correctness checks and API references below. MIT.

registry_skills.name: swiftui
registry_skills.note: SwiftUI API reference — views, layout, navigation, @State/@Binding/@Observable. MIT.

registry_skills.name: uikit
registry_skills.note: UIKit API reference, for the interop and legacy paths SwiftUI does not cover. MIT.

registry_skills.name: swift-testing
registry_skills.note: Swift Testing: @Test, @Suite, #expect, #require, traits, parameterized tests. MIT.

registry_skills.name: swift-concurrency
registry_skills.note: async/await, Task, TaskGroup, actors, AsyncSequence. MIT.

registry_skills.name: combine
registry_skills.note: Publishers and operators, for code that predates or interops with Swift concurrency. MIT.

registry_skills.name: apple-docs-index
registry_skills.note: Index of Apple developer documentation, for framework APIs not covered above. MIT.

registry_skills.name: xcuitest
registry_skills.note: UI test automation — the layer that actually exercises a running app. MIT.

registry_skills.name: simulator-utils
registry_skills.note: Driving and inspecting simulators without hand-typing simctl incantations. MIT.

approvals: archiving, submitting, or releasing anything to App Store Connect or TestFlight
any paid service, signing identity, provisioning profile, or App Store Connect API key
running anything on a physical device that touches Family Controls, Screen Time, HealthKit, camera, push, or location permissions
deleting branches, resetting git, wiping DerivedData, or removing untracked work
adding a third-party dependency to a project
